who_for: Most people need a laptop that's fast enough for browsing, documents, and video calls, lasts a full workday on battery, and is light enough to carry. That describes a mid-range model, not the most expensive one.
Pay more if you edit video or photos, play games, or need a premium build for daily travel. Students and casual users can save money with a budget model that has at least 8GB of RAM and an SSD.

how_we_picked.label: Performance
how_we_picked.text: We matched processor and RAM to real workloads. For most people 16GB of RAM is the comfortable target, and 8GB is the minimum.

how_we_picked.label: Battery life
how_we_picked.text: We weighed independent battery tests over manufacturer claims, favoring laptops that last a full workday.

how_we_picked.label: Display
how_we_picked.text: Screen brightness, resolution, and color matter for comfort and creative work, so we compared them alongside size.

how_we_picked.label: Keyboard and build
how_we_picked.text: A comfortable keyboard, a precise trackpad, and a sturdy chassis make a laptop pleasant to use for years.

how_we_picked.label: Ports and weight
how_we_picked.text: We checked for the ports you're likely to need, such as USB-C charging and USB-A, and how much each laptop weighs.
